content:
I want to encourage the use of Milestones within Physlib. Examples of these are given here. I hope that anyone is able to create them - if not please let me know.

They can be used to collect pull-requests and issues related to a similar topic, and thus can be used to easily point to contributions or track the progress of a given area.
Also if anyone has ideas of what Milestones we could create, please let me know.

if not please let me know.

I can see the two pre-existing Milestones but there is no button for me (as a contributer) to create a new one.

This is annoying and probably takes away a bit of the motivation of using it. Though maybe we could set up a GitHub workflow like we have with the labels to add-or-remove PRs from a given milestone. Doesn't solve the problem with creating milestones though.
Maybe encouraging the use of GitHub projects is a good alternative here then, since I think anyone can make their own project on their own account, and link to PRs in Physlib.

I've been thinking a bit more about this. I think the reason why something like milestones is not a good solution, is that it is dependent on technology not native to the project (i.e. it uses GitHub, pull-requests, issues etc.). That means that someone that can interact with the project may not be able to interact with the milestones etc.

I think there is another solution, which serves the same purpose.

  1. We make a directory .contributions/
  2. Within that we have files which detail the information of substantial contributions: Title, description, and a list of commits. Maybe also an author list, but that in theory is redundant information as it can be got (with a percentage of contribution) from the list of commits.

One could then build infrastructure to make it easy to 1) create such contribution files, and 2) view them. They would also give a more high-level but native way of understanding the history of the project.
